request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The rollup audit lines are in place, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works**
- A new `Rollup` service (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/Rollup.java`) works out each person's claimed and due-total on the server. It uses the same rules as the screen: only OPEN and SETTLED claims count, and a settled or stated claim keeps its fixed figure. A due-total is n/a when the person's grade has no rate today and no counting claim keeps a figure. The sheet totals add everyone up, skipping n/a.
- Every change endpoint now has a `TakeRollup` step that records the figures before anything is changed. These are: add person, edit person, set rate, add claim, edit claim, change a claim's status, take a statement, and change today. After the change's own audit line, it compares the figures before and after. It writes one `ROLLUP` line for each person whose figures moved (or who is new), in the order people were added. It then writes `TOTALS` only if the sheet totals moved.
- Changing today now has its own audit step that writes only these lines, never a line of its own. To know who made the change, `ValidateToday` now also passes on the `by` value from the request.
- A refused change stops before the audit step, so it writes nothing.

**Differs from the request:** the request says `ROLLUP name=<name>`, but the test expects `ROLLUP sheet=… by=… person=<name> claimed=… due-total=…`. I followed the test and used `person=`.

No front-end or database changes were needed.
